public_rationale: On 2025-08-20, Marcus wrote that the mania for LLMs "would break eventually." He gave no deadline. A Decrypt report available on 2025-08-20 quotes Sam Altman saying he thought investors were overexcited about AI (e3). That supports the idea that there was a mania. It does not show whether the mania later broke. Nvidia reported record revenue of $96.2 billion for the quarter ended July 26, 2026. That was up 106% from a year earlier. Data center revenue was $89.0 billion, up 117% (e1). On 2026-08-27, Nvidia's CEO said the AI infrastructure buildout was "at full steam" (e2). None of the evidence shows the sustained steep fall in AI spending that would settle this forecast early. The forecast has no deadline, so the lack of a collapse in the evidence does not count against it. It stays open.
limitations: The latest revenue figures in the evidence are for the quarter ended July 26, 2026. The evidence cannot show whether a collapse began between then and the 2026-10-28 evaluation date.
The only evidence dated after that quarter is the Nvidia CEO's statement of 2026-08-27, which is the company's own view.
The evidence has no data on hyperscaler AI capital spending, AI startup funding or valuations, or AI-linked stock indices.
All of the market evidence comes from one company, Nvidia.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The mania for LLMs will eventually break.

statement.excerpt: For the last few years, I have been warning you that the mania for LLMs would break eventually.
statement.document_title: Is this the moment when the Generative AI bubble finally deflates?

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at some point, enthusiasm for LLMs would visibly collapse. That means a sharp, sustained fall in generative AI investment, AI chip and data center spending, and AI-linked valuations, not a short dip.
He gave no deadline ('eventually'), so this is an open-horizon forecast. The lack of a collapse before the evaluation date does not count against him.
criteria.support_condition: A dated, decisive collapse of the LLM boom: for example, AI data center or chip spending falling steeply year over year for several quarters, major AI valuations or funding rounds collapsing, and widespread reporting that the boom has ended.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, the forecast cannot be shown false at a fixed date. Continued strong growth only shows the break has not happened yet.

evidence.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. reported record revenue for the second quarter ended July 26, 2026, of $96.2 billion, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 106% from a year ago.
evidence.locator: Summary, first paragraph after bullet points
evidence.explanation: The main seller of AI chips more than doubled its revenue year over year into mid-2026. That shows the LLM investment boom had not broken by then. It does not refute an open-ended forecast.

evidence.excerpt: The AI infrastructure buildout is at full steam.
evidence.explanation: Nvidia's CEO described the AI buildout as still accelerating in August 2026. This is a company view, but it is consistent with the reported revenue.

evidence.excerpt: “Are we in a phase where investors as a whole are overexcited about AI? My opinion is yes,” he said.
evidence.explanation: Even Altman said investors were overexcited around the time of the post. That backs the premise that there was a mania, but says nothing about whether it later broke.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated company filings or reputable financial reporting showing a sustained collapse. For example, Nvidia data center revenue or combined hyperscaler AI capital spending falling more than 30% year over year for two or more quarters in a row, together with broad reporting that generative AI investment has collapsed. That would support the forecast. Because there is no deadline, no fixed date can contradict it.
